claims.content: C2 JU terminates and purges surveillance tracks (Air, Surface/Maritime, Land/Ground) by transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message or by automatically purging remote tracks after a specific time interval.

scope_contract.goal_statement: C2 JU terminates and purges surveillance tracks (Air, Surface/Maritime, Land/Ground) by transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message or by automatically purging remote tracks after a specific time interval.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: C2 JU terminates and purges a selected surveillance track by transmitting a J7.0 message with ACT = 0.
scope_contract.start_boundary: A surveillance track exists and C2 JU is ready to terminate and purge it.
scope_contract.success_boundary: The selected surveillance track has been terminated and purged via the J7.0 (ACT = 0) transmission.
in_scope_actions: Transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message to terminate a surveillance track
Automatically purging remote tracks after a specific time interval
Terminating surveillance tracks in Air, Surface/Maritime, and Land/Ground categories
excluded_adjacent_actions: Using PPLI data from J2 messages to reduce redundancy of surveillance track reporting
Terminating EW product information transmission when the information is no longer valid or time-related update requirements are not met
Post-purge reporting, dissemination, or downstream track-management actions
variant_dimensions: Track category: Air, Surface/Maritime, Land/Ground, ballistic missile
Termination mechanism: explicit J7.0 (ACT = 0) message vs automatic timeout-based remote track purge

claims.content: C2 JU
For the explicit J7.0 (ACT = 0) termination path, the C2 JU currently has reporting responsibility (R²) for the surveillance track that is to be terminated.
For automatic purging, a remote track exists for which no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been received and no further updates have occurred.

The use case is triggered when C2 JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has reporting responsibility, initiating transmission of a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report, or when a remote track has received no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and no further updates, and the specified time interval since its last report elapses, triggering automatic purge.

Two trigger conditions begin the main flow: (1) a C2 JU ceases reporting a track for which it currently has reporting responsibility (R²) and transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message, except when the track becomes an active IU on the network with the same address as the reference TN or, for a ballistic missile track, when relinquishing R² to another JU; or (2) a C2 JU receives no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and no further updates on a remote track for a specific time interval, after which the system shall have the capability to automatically purge those tracks.
C2 JU transmits a J7.0 Track Management message with the Track Management Action (ACT) field set to value 0 (Drop Track Report) for the Reference TN of the ceased track.
The J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message indicates that the C2 JU has dropped or has ceased reporting the track specified in the Reference TN field.
For segmented lines or multisided areas defined by more than one Reference TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall be transmitted for each Reference TN.

Diverges from Step 2: Instead of transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message, C2 JU automatically purges a remote track after a specified time interval has elapsed since the track's last report, when no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message has been received and no further updates on the remote track have occurred; the automatic purge applies to track types DRT = 0-3, and DATUMS (DRT = 4) shall not be purged automatically.

Diverges from Step 2: For a remote ballistic missile track on which no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received and no further updates occur, C2 JU automatically purges the track after a system-selected time interval.

Diverges from main_flow Step 2: if the system does not receive a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and receives no further updates on a remote track, the track may be automatically purged after a system-selected time interval; under this automatic-purge condition, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message shall not be transmitted. Exit: go to the automatic-purge alternative flow.

Diverges from main_flow Step 2: if the simulation status of a track is to be changed for any reason, such as operator error, the track shall be dropped using the J7.0 (ACT = 0) message and a new track shall be reported. Exit: J7.0 (ACT = 0) drop is performed, followed by reporting a new track.

For the explicit termination path, the C2 JU has transmitted a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track Report message for the track identified in the Reference TN field, and the C2 JU has dropped or has ceased reporting that track.

For the automatic-purge path, a remote track/point (DRT 0-3) for which no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message was received and no further updates occurred has been purged after the system-selected time interval elapsed.
When a remote track/point is automatically purged, the C2 JU does not transmit a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message for that track.

For the automatic-purge path involving a remote ballistic missile track, the track has been purged after the system-selected time interval when no J7.0 (ACT = 0) message was received and no further updates occurred.

quality_flags.detail: [mainflow_postconditions_reachability] The trigger and postconditions define an automatic-purge path, but the main flow contains no steps for automatic purging of remote tracks/points. Steps 1-3 only cover explicit J7.0 (ACT=0) termination, and step 4 is an exclusion for cases where J7.0 is not sent. Therefore the automatic-purge postconditions (remote track/point purged, no J7.0 sent, ballistic track auto-purged) are unreachable from the main flow. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (The actual automatic purge of non-ballistic remote tracks/points is not supported by the cited cards; only the capability/permission to purge is supported.))

[mainflow_postconditions_reachability] Main Flow step 1 opens with two trigger conditions, one of which is automatic purge of a remote track after a timeout, but step 2 unconditionally states 'C2 JU transmits a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message'. The automatic-purge postconditions require that the track is purged without transmitting J7.0, so the main flow as written sends a J7.0 for both paths and does not lead to the automatic-purge postconditions.

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger states that the use case is triggered whenever C2 JU ceases reporting a track it is responsible for and initiates J7.0 (ACT = 0). Main Flow step 1 adds exceptions for when the track becomes an active IU on the network with the same address as the reference TN, and for a ballistic missile track when R² is relinquished to another JU. These exceptions are absent from the Trigger, so the Trigger is broader than the actual main flow and would start the use case in cases where the main flow says a J7.0 shall not be transmitted.

inconsistency_hints: Precondition 2 states that the specified time interval since the track's last report has already elapsed, but the automatic-purge trigger is the elapsing of that interval. This puts the trigger event into the preconditions, so the automatic-purge path cannot start with a pending timer; the state before the trigger should be a qualifying remote track/point with no J7.0/no updates and the interval still being monitored.

Main flow step 4 is an exception, not a main success step: it says C2 JU does not transmit J7.0 (ACT=0) when ceasing reporting because the track becomes an Active IU with the same TN or because R² is relinquished. This conflicts with step 2 and postcondition 1, which require J7.0 transmission for the explicit termination path, and leaves those cases without a defined postcondition.

Precondition 1 is stated without a path scope and appears to require R² for all entries to the use case. The automatic-purge trigger applies to remote tracks that have received no J7.0 (ACT=0) and no updates; those tracks are not necessarily under the C2 JU's reporting responsibility. The un-scoped R² precondition can prevent the automatic trigger from being valid.

Precondition 2 includes the condition that the specified time interval has already elapsed, but the trigger is the elapsing of that same interval. Before the trigger fires, the interval has not yet elapsed, so this clause duplicates the trigger event instead of stating a pre-existing state.

Main Flow step 1 is written for the explicit J7.0 trigger only. The trigger also defines an automatic timeout-based purge path, but for that path C2 JU is not ceasing reporting for an R² track. The main flow then places the automatic-purge behavior as step 4 after the explicit J7.0 flow, making the two mutually exclusive paths read as one linear sequence.

Main_flow step 4 already states the automatic-purge scenario: C2 JU purges a remote track if no J7.0 (ACT = 0) is received and no updates occur, and in that case no J7.0 is transmitted. The alternative_flow then claims the same scenario as a divergence from Step 2, so it is not a genuine divergence from the main flow; the automatic-purge branch is duplicated in the anchor slot.
